title: 搭讪开场的松驰感，别再背收号台词了

timeline.summary: Case one: a man compliments a woman's Matrix-like outfit, identifies the interaction as an approach, and they discuss the surprise or fear caused by a stranger suddenly speaking.

He says he hesitated for about 30 seconds. After she asks to use the restroom, he proposes exchanging WeChat; later dialogue mentions not normally adding contacts and his interpretation of a green light before goodbye.
A hard cut starts case two with a different woman and companion. He asks about shopping, compliments clothing, says he wants to meet, and requests WeChat.
Case two continues through origin, student status, busy schedule and a future outing proposal, followed by brief assent and goodbye.
No reliable ASR; ending does not verify a saved contact or future meeting.

claims.speaker: first approached woman, attribution from dialogue context
claims.statement: She says a stranger suddenly speaking can feel frightening or startling.
claims.conditions: Localized participant feedback, not a universal response; it supports keeping approaches visible, low-pressure and easy to end.

claims.speaker: field man
claims.statement: He names his intent to meet and uses situational clothing compliments rather than a hidden pretext in both cases.
claims.conditions: Direct intent does not override a request to leave, discomfort or refusal.

claims.speaker: field participants, turns partly uncertain
claims.statement: When the first woman asks to go to the restroom, the man converts the interaction into a contact request and later labels the exception as a green light.
claims.conditions: A need to leave takes priority. Brief assent or an exception to a contact rule is not broader romantic or ongoing consent.

claims.speaker: field participants, turns partly uncertain
claims.statement: In the second case, basic information exchange proceeds to a future outing proposal and a short affirmative response.
claims.conditions: Edited speech and unreadable phone actions do not prove contact exchange or that the future outing occurred.

examples.summary: Two distinct public interactions are joined by a hard cut around 74.88 seconds and must not be combined into one successful progression.

speaker_attribution.speaker: field man
speaker_attribution.basis: Same male participant across both cases, but formal source did not independently prove he is Mikey; retain role attribution.

speaker_attribution.speaker: first approached woman
speaker_attribution.basis: Black-coat participant visible in frames 000001-000002; precise short turns remain non-diarized.

speaker_attribution.speaker: second approached woman and companion
speaker_attribution.basis: Different pair visible after the hard cut and in frame 000003; do not merge with case one.

visual_findings: All three sampled frames were reviewed. Frames 000001-000002 show the first black-coat participant; frame 000003 shows a different woman with a companion, confirming two separate cases.
Faces and shopping context are visible. Holding a phone does not establish contact saving or later communication.
The samples do not show a complete leave sequence, a readable phone screen or a future outing.

permissions.reason: Duplicate formal source; contact, departure, speaker, privacy and outcome boundaries remain unresolved.

limitations: Automatic transcript was not word-for-word audio checked or diarized.
Three sparse frames do not equal continuous audio-visual review.
The two cases are edited and their contact/follow-up outcomes are not verified.
Filming and publication consent for participants and bystanders are unknown.
